requirement:
The generated test MUST carry the `{test}` annotation for the built-in `habeas:validate` under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. Only `{test}` may reference this built-in. Its fixed text is

> The project’s Cargo integration test must call `habeas::validate()` to check its requirements and evidence.

Rerunning setup MUST upgrade the exact unannotated test generated by previous versions and MUST preserve user edits as required by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup`.
rationale:
structural: Every clause of `requirements.cli.setup.validation_test` specifies observable output or behavior, not how the code is built. The clauses are: the generated test carries the `{test}` annotation for `habeas:validate`; only `{test}` may reference this built-in; the fixed text of the built-in; and rerunning setup upgrades the exact unannotated legacy test and preserves user edits. None names a library, algorithm, signature, type, or delegation through a named interface. An implementation could build the file content with `format!`, a template file, or `include_str!` instead of a `const`. It would write the same bytes and still satisfy the text, so the choice of a `const` is discretionary. The same holds for the upgrade and preserve logic, which only needs to produce the right file contents.

The supplied root `src/setup.rs#const[TEST_SOURCE]` holds the annotated test content (`// {test}`habeas:validate``, then `#[test] fn habeas() { habeas::validate(); }`). `src/setup.rs#const[LEGACY_TEST_SOURCE]` is the exact unannotated legacy text. `src/setup.rs#fn[run]` pairs the two when it writes `tests/habeas.rs`. This is consistent with the requirement, but I judged it only as context, not as a structural obligation. Whether the behavior is verified belongs to the behavioral criterion, so I report no structural gap.

behavioral: Obligations and the tests that cover them:

1. **The generated test carries the `{test}` annotation for `habeas:validate`.** `tests/setup.rs#fn[setup_is_repeatable]` runs setup twice on a fresh fixture. It asserts that `tests/habeas.rs` is exactly `// {test}`habeas:validate`\n#[test]\nfn habeas() {...}`. It then runs `validate` on the result. `tests/setup.rs#fn[setup_upgrades_the_previous_generated_validation_test]` asserts the same exact content after an upgrade.

2. **Fixed text, and only `{test}` may reference the built-in.** `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validation_test_builtin_matches_the_reference_and_permits_only_tests]` has three assertions:
   - The built-in's text equals the quoted text in `md/reference.md`.
   - `roles` equals `[ReferenceKind::Test]`.
   - `check(Test)` is ok.
   The roles equality enforces that no other role is permitted. Reporting of disallowed roles is the job of `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, which is cited context and is not reassessed here.

3. **Rerunning setup upgrades the exact unannotated test generated by previous versions.** `setup_upgrades_the_previous_generated_validation_test` writes the old unannotated generated content, runs setup, and asserts the file becomes the annotated version.

4. **Rerunning setup preserves user edits, as `requirements.cli.setup` requires.** `setup_does_not_overwrite_a_differing_test_or_stylesheet` writes a user-modified `tests/habeas.rs`. The modification is a comment added to the otherwise old content. Setup must fail with an "already exists with different content" message that names the file. The file content must stay unchanged, and `book.toml` and `Cargo.toml` must stay unchanged too. `setup_is_repeatable` covers a rerun on the already annotated file.

The tests assert outcomes and distinguish the cases the text names: a fresh file, the exact old generated file, and an edited file. I found no unaddressed behavioral obligation.

text: :::{req} setup.validation_test

The generated test MUST carry the `{test}` annotation for the built-in `habeas:validate` under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. Only `{test}` may reference this built-in. Its fixed text is
> The project’s Cargo integration test must call `habeas::validate()` to check its requirements and evidence.
Rerunning setup MUST upgrade the exact unannotated test generated by previous versions and MUST preserve user edits as required by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup`.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas provides built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in has fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation,
and states which reference roles may use it. References resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, a
built-in reference displayed under {cite}`requirements.references.book_badges`
uses a badge without a link whose hover text gives the built-in's full text.
Built-ins themselves neither require nor permit definition evidence files and
do not appear as definitions in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of
{cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. Per-source citation reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` may be required for references
to a built-in. A project definition cannot use a full name beginning with
`habeas:`; validation reports one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation reports a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} setup

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and preserve customized tests and stylesheets. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
